extracted.intended_audience: public water systems (community and noncommunity), water utility operators, and State drinking water regulators implementing Cryptosporidium treatment requirements
extracted.subtask_description: Federal regulatory requirements for determining Cryptosporidium levels, required inactivation/removal, eligible treatment credits (microbial toolbox), monitoring, challenge and integrity testing, reporting, and schedules for public water systems to meet treatment technique requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of mean Cryptosporidium level
rubrics_metrics.description: Unfiltered systems must calculate the arithmetic mean of all Cryptosporidium sample concentrations reported under §§141.701(a) (initial) and §141.701(b) (second round) and report this value to the State for approval no later than 6 months after the month the system is required to complete the applicable monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If sampling frequency varies, first calculate a monthly average for each month and use the monthly averages (not individual samples) to compute the mean. The report to the State must include a summary of the source water monitoring data used for the calculation. Failure to comply is a violation of the treatment technique requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cryptosporidium inactivation requirements by mean level
rubrics_metrics.description: Unfiltered systems must provide Cryptosporidium inactivation based on mean Cryptosporidium level: systems with mean ≤ 0.01 oocysts/L must provide at least 2-log inactivation; systems with mean > 0.01 oocysts/L must provide at least 3-log inactivation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These inactivation levels apply according to the compliance schedule in §141.713.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inactivation treatment technology requirements (unfiltered systems)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unfiltered systems must use chlorine dioxide, ozone, or UV as described in §141.720 to meet Cryptosporidium inactivation requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems using chlorine dioxide or ozone that fail to achieve required inactivation on more than one day in a calendar month are in violation. Systems using UV that fail to meet the criteria in §141.720(d)(3)(ii) are in violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of two disinfectants requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Unfiltered systems must meet combined Cryptosporidium inactivation and Giardia lamblia and virus inactivation requirements using a minimum of two disinfectants, and each of the two disinfectants must separately achieve the total inactivation required for either Cryptosporidium, Giardia lamblia, or viruses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule for compliance with Cryptosporidium treatment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Filtered and unfiltered systems must provide required Cryptosporidium treatment according to the schedule in §141.713. Compliance dates vary by system size: ≥100,000 people by April 1, 2012; 50,000–99,999 by Oct 1, 2012; 10,000–49,999 by Oct 1, 2013; fewer than 10,000 by Oct 1, 2014.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may allow up to an additional two years for systems making capital improvements. If bin classification or mean level changes after the second round of monitoring, the State-approved schedule applies for meeting any new treatment level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for uncovered finished water storage facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems using uncovered finished water storage facilities must notify the State of each such facility by April 1, 2008, and must either cover each facility or treat discharge to the distribution system to achieve ≥4-log virus, ≥3-log Giardia lamblia, and ≥2-log Cryptosporidium by April 1, 2009 (or be on a State-approved schedule to meet these conditions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply is a violation of the treatment technique requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and use of microbial toolbox options
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems receive treatment credits listed in the microbial toolbox table by meeting the conditions in §§141.716–141.720, and apply these credits to meet treatment requirements in §141.711 or §141.712 as applicable. Unfiltered systems are eligible only for the microbial toolbox options described in §141.720.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The toolbox groups options into source protection/management, pre-filtration, treatment performance, additional filtration, and inactivation categories with specified log credits and criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Watershed control program criteria (0.5-log credit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems implementing a State-approved watershed control program that meets the section's requirements receive 0.5-log Cryptosporidium treatment credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be eligible, systems must notify the State of intent no later than two years prior to the system's treatment compliance date and submit a proposed watershed control plan at least one year before the date. The plan must identify an 'area of influence', identify potential and actual sources of Cryptosporidium/fecal contamination and assess relative impacts, analyze effectiveness/feasibility of control measures, and include goals, specific actions, partners, resources, and an implementation schedule. Existing programs (in place Jan 5, 2006) may seek credit if plans meet criteria. If the State does not respond to a submitted plan, the program is considered approved unless withdrawn. To maintain credit systems must: submit annual program status reports describing implementation and adequacy; undergo a watershed sanitary survey every three years (community) or five years (noncommunity) meeting State guidelines; and make plan and reports available to the public in plain language (with limited withholding allowed for security). The State may withdraw credit if the system is not carrying out the approved plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative source/intake management criteria (no prescribed credit)
rubrics_metrics.description: A system may conduct alternative source monitoring (different intake location or different timing/level of withdrawal) and, with State approval, determine its bin classification based on such results; no prescribed credit is assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems conducting alternative source monitoring must concurrently monitor their current plant intake as described in §141.701, meet the source monitoring requirements in §§141.701–141.706, report alternative monitoring results and supporting operating condition documentation to the State, and, if bin classification is determined by alternative monitoring, relocate the intake or permanently adopt the withdrawal procedure by the applicable compliance date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presedimentation basin criteria (0.5-log credit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems receive 0.5-log Cryptosporidium treatment credit during any month a presedimentation basin meets criteria: continuous operation treating entire plant flow from a surface water or GWUDI source, continuous coagulant addition, and achievement of specified performance criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance criteria are either (i) demonstrate at least 0.5-log mean reduction of influent turbidity calculated as log10(monthly mean influent turbidity) − log10(monthly mean effluent turbidity) using daily turbidity measurements, or (ii) meet State-approved performance criteria demonstrating ≥0.5-log mean removal of micron-sized particulate material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-stage lime softening criteria (0.5-log additional credit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems receive an additional 0.5-log Cryptosporidium treatment credit for two-stage lime softening if chemical addition and hardness precipitation occur in two separate and sequential softening stages prior to filtration and both stages treat the entire plant flow from a surface water or GWUDI source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single-stage softening is credited as equivalent to conventional treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bank filtration eligibility and performance criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Bank filtration serving as pretreatment to a filtration plant receives treatment credit: wells with ≥25-foot groundwater flow path receive 0.5-log; wells with ≥50-foot receive 1.0-log. Only wells in granular aquifers and only horizontal/vertical wells are eligible (springs/infiltration galleries are not eligible here).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aquifer characterization requires extraction of a core demonstrating that in ≥90% of core length grains <1.0 mm diameter constitute at least 10% of core material. Groundwater flow path measurement differs by well type (vertical: distance from edge of surface water under high flow conditions; horizontal: distance from river bed under normal flow to closest lateral screen). Systems must monitor each wellhead for turbidity at least once every 4 hours while bank filtration is in operation; if monthly average turbidity (based on daily maxima) exceeds 1 NTU, report to State and conduct assessment within 30 days. If State determines microbial removal compromised, State may revoke credit until corrective actions approved. The State may approve greater credit based on a State-approved demonstration of performance study sampling production and monitoring wells and collecting hydrogeologic/water quality data across operating conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combined filter performance criteria (0.5-log credit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems using conventional or direct filtration receive 0.5-log credit during months when combined filter effluent (CFE) turbidity is ≤ 0.15 NTU in at least 95% of measurements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Turbidity must be measured as described in §141.74(a) and (c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual filter performance criteria (0.5-log additional credit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems using conventional or direct filtration receive an additional 0.5-log credit if individual filter effluent turbidity is ≤ 0.15 NTU in at least 95% of samples each month in each filter and is never > 0.3 NTU in two consecutive measurements in any filter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance is based on individual filter turbidity monitoring per §141.174 or §141.560. If a system that has received this credit fails the requirements during any month, the State may determine that the failure was due to unusual short-term circumstances not reasonably preventable and that no more than two such failures occurred in a calendar year; in that case the system does not receive a treatment technique violation under §141.711(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstration of performance studies (state-approved) for treatment credit
rubrics_metrics.description: The State may approve Cryptosporidium treatment credit for processes based on a demonstration of performance study that follows a State-approved protocol and demonstrates the level of reduction under the full range of expected operating conditions. Credit may be greater or less than prescribed credits and may be awarded to processes that do not meet prescribed criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any toolbox option included in a demonstration study cannot also receive the prescribed toolbox credit. State approval must be in writing and may include monitoring and performance criteria that the system must demonstrate and report on an ongoing basis to remain eligible; the State may designate verification criteria to ensure approved conditions are maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bag and cartridge filter challenge testing and credit assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems receive up to 2.0-log credit for individual bag/cartridge filters and up to 2.5-log for filters in series if they meet challenge testing and reporting criteria; filters must treat the entire plant flow from a subpart H source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenge testing must be on full-scale filters and housings identical in material and construction to those used in service and in the same configuration (individual or series). Testing must use Cryptosporidium or a surrogate removed no more efficiently than Cryptosporidium and the challenge particulate concentration must be determined by a method that discretely quantifies that organism (turbidity not allowed). Maximum feed concentration = 1 × 10^4 × (filtrate detection limit). Tests must be at maximum design flow, for durations sufficient to reach 100% of terminal pressure drop. LRV = log10(Cf) − log10(Cp) with Cp set equal to detection limit if not detected. Each filter must be challenged during three periods (within 2 hours of startup, when pressure drop 45–55% of terminal, and at end of cycle at 100% terminal); the filter LRV is the minimum of the three. If <20 filters tested, product-line efficiency = lowest LRV_filter; if ≥20 then = 10th percentile (i/(n+1)). Modifications that could change removal efficiency require new challenge testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membrane filtration credit determination and challenge testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Membrane filtration receives log credit equal to the lower of (i) removal efficiency demonstrated during challenge testing and (ii) the maximum removal efficiency verifiable through direct integrity testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenge testing must be on full-scale or smaller-scale modules identical in material and similar in construction to full-scale. Tests must use Cryptosporidium oocysts or an appropriate surrogate, with concentrations determined by discrete quantification methods. Maximum feed concentration = 3.16 × 10^6 × (filtrate detection limit). Testing must be under representative hydraulic conditions at maximum design flux and maximum design process recovery. LRV calculation and LRV_C-Test determination follow the same per-module and percentile rules as other challenge testing (lowest if <20, 10th percentile if ≥20). The challenge test must establish a QCRV (quality control release value) for a non-destructive performance test to verify removal capability on production modules; production modules not meeting QCRV are not eligible for the credit. Modifications to the membrane that could change removal efficiency or QCRV require additional challenge testing and new QCRV determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct integrity testing requirements for membrane units
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct integrity testing must demonstrate removal efficiency equal to or greater than the removal credit awarded and meet specified requirements: independently applied to each membrane unit, resolution ≤ 3 micrometers, and sensitivity sufficient to verify the log treatment credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sensitivity (LRV_DIT) must be calculated either using pressure/vacuum test equation LRV_DIT = LOG10(Qp / (VCF × Q_breach)) where Qp = total design filtrate flow, Q_breach = flow from smallest measurable integrity breach, VCF = volumetric concentration factor; or using marker method LRV_DIT = LOG10(Cf) − LOG10(Cp) where Cf and Cp are feed and filtrate concentrations of the marker. Systems must establish control limits within the sensitivity limits that indicate an integral membrane unit capable of meeting the awarded credit. If a direct integrity test result exceeds the control limit, the unit must be removed from service, repairs verified by direct integrity test before return to service. Direct integrity testing frequency: at least once each day the membrane unit is in operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting, State approval, and documentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple provisions require reporting to and approval by the State: reporting mean Cryptosporidium levels (within 6 months), submitting watershed control plans (1 year before compliance date) and annual status reports, reporting alternative source monitoring and operating conditions, reporting challenge testing results for bag/cartridge and membrane filters, and notifying the State of uncovered finished water storage facilities (by April 1, 2008) and intent to seek watershed credit (two years prior).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State approval (explicit written approval or deemed approval if State does not respond) is required for many credits; the State may set ongoing monitoring/performance criteria as conditions of approval and may withdraw credit for non-compliance. Certain documents must be made available to the public in plain language unless the State approves withholding for security reasons.
